 Bavuma backs Hamza at number three against Bangladesh
 Dustin Wetdewich 
 | 
 15 Nov 2026

 Zubayr Hamza will end a wait of more than two years when he walks out for South Africa against Bangladesh in the first Test at the Wanderers Stadium on Sunday.
 ALSO READ: Bavuma set to extend record start as South Africa host Bangladesh 
 Captain Temba Bavuma confirmed the 31-year-old will bat at number three, taking over from David Bedingham after his axing following last month’s series against Australia.
 Seamer Dane Paterson comes in for Gerald Coetzee in the only other switch from the side that sealed the Australia series with a 176-run victory in the third Test in Cape Town.
 ALSO READ: How does cricket’s World Test Championship work?  
 Fast bowler Anrich Nortje, who featured in the first two Tests against Australia, remains in the squad but has not yet shaken off a groin injury, according to Bavuma.
 Off-spinner Simon Harmer keeps his place as the lone specialist slow bowler, with man-of-the-match honours in Cape Town underpinning his selection ahead of long-serving first-choice Keshav Maharaj.
 Hamza’s most recent Test appearance came in an under-strength South African line-up on tour in New Zealand in 2023/24, and he has not featured in a home Test since the visit of England in January 2020.
 Hamza served a nine-month suspension in 2022 after a positive test for a banned substance, which he attributed to mistakenly taking medication prescribed for his father.
 “He has gone back and done what he can in domestic cricket,” said Bavuma. “He’s scored runs in all formats.”
 The Gauteng Lions, the team Hamza represents domestically, call the Wanderers home.
 Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said he would finalise his XI on the morning of the match, but expected to field three pace bowlers alongside one specialist spinner.
 “I think I can say that there will be three pacers,” said Shanto. “There must also be a spinner.”
 Shanto acknowledged South Africa would start as strong favourites but drew confidence from his side’s recent showings and a one-day series triumph in the country in 2021/22.
 Bavuma, meanwhile, stressed the need for the world Test champions to keep their standards high as they build towards the next final in 2027.
 “We are halfway on our journey and we are still looking at ways we can improve,” he said.
